options.text: Carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide to form insoluble calcium carbonate, which makes the liquid look milky.
Oxygen from the reaction reacts with calcium hydroxide to make the liquid milky.
The milky look is the calcium hydroxide itself becoming visible, with no new solid formed.
Any gas from the kitchen reaction turns lime water milky, including water vapour alone.

stem:
Mehak bubbles the gas from a baking-soda and vinegar reaction through a test tube of clear lime water. After a short time the liquid turns milky.

Which claim is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: CO2 reacts with calcium hydroxide to form insoluble calcium carbonate (milky). Oxygen or water vapour alone is not the lime-water test gas; milkiness is the new solid, not the hydroxide itself.
